title.en: Follow the argument line by line
title.es: Seguir el hilo de un argumento

es: Distinguir tesis, evidencia, objeción y réplica en un debate escuchado y ordenarlas en un esquema.

teaching.en: My claim is that cars should stay out of the town centre on Sundays.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es que los coches deberían quedarse fuera del centro de la ciudad los domingos.
teaching.explanationEs: My claim is that… anuncia lo que el hablante defiende: es la tesis del argumento.
segments: My claim is that cars should stay
out of the town centre on Sundays.
teaching.audioText: My claim is that cars should stay out of the town centre on Sundays.

teaching.en: The evidence is a survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.
teaching.es: La evidencia es una encuesta: el sesenta por ciento de los clientes prefiere una calle tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: La evidencia es un dato que se puede comprobar: una encuesta, una cifra, un hecho.
segments: The evidence is a survey: sixty per
cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is a survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.

teaching.en: In my opinion the street is nicer without traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, la calle es más agradable sin tráfico, pero una opinión no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Una opinión dice lo que piensas; la evidencia muestra por qué los demás deberían creerte.
segments: In my opinion the street is nicer without
traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion the street is nicer without traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.

teaching.en: One objection is that older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.
teaching.es: Una objeción es que las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos; la réplica es que autobuses gratuitos las llevarán.
teaching.explanationEs: La objeción es el argumento contrario y la réplica (rebuttal) responde a esa objeción.
segments: One objection is that older people cannot walk far;
the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.
teaching.audioText: One objection is that older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.

teaching.en: The survey figures support the claim, because they come from shoppers, not from me.
teaching.es: Las cifras de la encuesta respaldan la tesis, porque vienen de los clientes y no de mí.
teaching.explanationEs: Support the claim: la evidencia respalda la tesis y la hace creíble.
segments: The survey figures support the claim, because
they come from shoppers, not from me.
teaching.audioText: The survey figures support the claim, because they come from shoppers, not from me.

teaching.en: An outline of the debate has three boxes: the claim, the evidence and the objection.
teaching.es: Un esquema del debate tiene tres casillas: la tesis, la evidencia y la objeción.
teaching.explanationEs: Al escuchar, rellenas mentalmente un esquema con estas piezas en orden.
segments: An outline of the debate has three boxes:
the claim, the evidence and the objection.
teaching.audioText: An outline of the debate has three boxes: the claim, the evidence and the objection.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pieza del argumento es la frase del texto?

choices.text: Evidence
An objection
A claim

feedback.es: «My claim is that…» anuncia lo que el hablante defiende, es decir, la tesis.

hint.es: Pregúntate si es lo que defiende o un dato que lo prueba.

origin.text: My claim is that schools should start later.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según la encuesta, el 70 % de los alumnos duerme poco.»

feedback.es: According to presenta la fuente de un dato, que es lo que convierte una idea en evidencia.

hint.es: Es la palabra con la que se cita una fuente.

origin.text: ___ to the survey, seventy per cent of pupils sleep too little.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La evidencia muestra que los alumnos duermen poco.»

answer.text: The evidence shows that pupils sleep too little

feedback.es: Evidence es incontable: lleva verbo en singular (shows) y no admite -s.

hint.es: Evidence no lleva -s y el verbo va en singular.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la tesis de la hablante.

choices.text: The town should plant more trees.
Streets with trees are cooler in summer.
Trees need a lot of water.

feedback.es: La tesis es «I am arguing that…»; el dato de los cuatro grados es evidencia y lo del agua, una objeción.

origin.audio: I am arguing that our town should plant more trees. The evidence is simple: streets with trees are four degrees cooler in summer. Some people object that trees need water.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del texto es evidencia y no opinión?

choices.text: I think the new library is great.
The survey found that four hundred students visited it in May.
It feels like the best place in town.

feedback.es: Solo la primera frase cita una fuente y una cifra comprobable; las otras dos expresan gusto personal.

origin.text: I think the new library is great. The survey found that four hundred students visited it in May. It feels like the best place in town.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con su pieza.

pairs: My claim is that buses should be free.
The survey shows that most riders are students.
One objection is that the council has no money.
The rebuttal is that full buses save money.

feedback.es: Cada pieza tiene su señal: My claim, The survey shows, One objection y The rebuttal.

pairs: My claim is that buses should be free.
The survey shows that most riders are students.
One objection is that the council has no money.
The rebuttal is that full buses save money.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la evidencia que aporta el equipo.

choices.text: Drivers lose space on the road.
Cyclists need their own lane.
Accidents went down where towns built bike lanes.

feedback.es: La evidencia es el dato sobre los accidentes; la pérdida de espacio es la objeción y lo de los carriles es la tesis.

origin.audio: Our claim is that cyclists need their own lane. The evidence is simple: accidents fell by a third where towns built one. Of course, drivers object that a lane takes space from cars.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué responde la hablante a la objeción.

choices.text: That a museum costs less than a new road.
That a new road serves more people.
That visitors pay for the museum themselves.

feedback.es: La réplica responde a la objeción del coste comparando el museo con una carretera nueva.

origin.audio: Some people object that free museums are expensive. The rebuttal is that one museum costs less than a new road, and it serves many more people.

prompt.es: Elige la tesis que falta en el esquema.

choices.text: Sixty per cent of parents answered.
Pupils should keep their uniforms.
Uniforms limit personal style.

feedback.es: La tesis es lo que defiende todo el esquema: la encuesta la respalda y la objeción la cuestiona.

origin.text: Outline. Claim: ___. Evidence: a survey says sixty per cent of parents find uniforms cheaper. Objection: pupils cannot choose their own style.

prompt.es: Escribe la tesis y la evidencia de este debate.

answer.text: My claim is that shops should close on Sundays. According to a survey, sixty-five per cent of employees prefer to rest that day.
accepted: My claim is that shops should close on Sundays. According to a survey, sixty-five per cent of employees prefer to rest that day.
I am arguing that shops should close on Sundays. The survey shows that 65 per cent of employees prefer to rest that day.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta separa la tesis (My claim is that…) de la evidencia con su fuente (According to…).

origin.text: Debate: ¿deben cerrar las tiendas los domingos? Tu tesis: sí. Tu evidencia: según una encuesta, el 65 % de los empleados prefiere descansar ese día.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pieza es la frase final del texto?

choices.text: A claim
Evidence
A rebuttal

feedback.es: La frase final responde a la objeción de los vecinos, así que es una réplica.

origin.text: Some neighbours say a Sunday market would be noisy. The organisers reply that the market would close at two.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una opinión no es una prueba.»

feedback.es: Una opinión expresa lo que piensas, mientras que la evidencia aporta datos comprobables.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué duda la hablante.

choices.text: Whether the survey is big enough to prove the claim.
Whether twenty people answered honestly.
Whether the plan will cost too much.

feedback.es: La objeción va contra el tamaño de la muestra: veinte personas no bastan como evidencia.

origin.audio: I object to the plan for one reason. The survey asked only twenty people, and twenty people are not enough evidence.
